title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates the 9th two-day National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference-2026 in New Delhi
body_text:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Co-operation Shri Amit Shah inaugurated the 9th two-day National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference-2026 in New Delhi today.
Prior to the inauguration, Union Home Minister paid homage at the Martyrs’ column by laying a wreath in remembrance of the brave personnel of Intelligence Bureau who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty to safeguardnational security and integrity.
The Conference held in hybrid format was attended by over 850 participants from across the country. Ministers of State for Home Affairs, Union Home Secretary, Deputy NSAs, Heads of CAPFs/CPOs attended the conference in Delhi. DGsP of States and UTs, young police officers working at the cutting-edge level and domain experts from specialised fields joined the conference through virtual mode.
On the first day of the Conference, discussions focused on critical aspects of national security, including response to counter-terrorism challenges, fusion, analysis and operationalisation of intelligence through the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), vision document on narcotics control, detection & deportation of illegal migrants, a policy framework to combat cyber-crime and proxy warfare by Pakistan.
For effective tackling of terrorism & radicalisation, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah emphasised on training for implementation of MHA’s PRAHAAR scheme, expediting trial by bringing back fugitives & using trial in absentia provisions and undertaking comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating UAPA cases. The Home Minister directed that an AI-based analysis of information available on MAC platforms should be done to create SOPs to counter various national security challenges. Union Home Minister directed all the agencies to take strict measures against infiltration.
The second day of the Conference will focus on the threat landscape from sub-aerial systems and formulating countermeasures, securing the blue economy, information warfare and its implications on national security and the need for a bio-security framework.
In pursuance to the directions of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, NSSC is being held every year in hybrid format since 2021, with the objective of finding solutions to major National Security Challenges using the extensive experience of cutting-edge level officers working at the grass roots level in collaboration with domain experts.

enrichment.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the 9th National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference-2026 in New Delhi, a hybrid-format event attended by over 850 participants including CAPF chiefs, DGsP, Deputy NSAs and young police officers. Day one covered counter-terrorism, intelligence fusion through the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), narcotics control, illegal migration, cyber-crime policy and Pakistan-sponsored proxy warfare, with Shah directing AI-based analysis of MAC data and implementation of the PRAHAAR scheme. Day two will address sub-aerial threats, blue economy security, information warfare and bio-security frameworks.
enrichment.context: The National Security Strategies Conference has been held annually since 2021 on the Prime Minister's directive to bring together grassroots-level police officers and domain experts to address emerging security challenges collaboratively. The Multi Agency Centre (MAC), operational since the post-26/11 reforms, is India's key mechanism for real-time intelligence sharing among central and state agencies to prevent terror attacks. PRAHAAR is an MHA scheme aimed at strengthening capacity to counter radicalisation and terrorism at the grassroots. The conference's agenda—covering cyber-crime, narcotics, illegal migration, blue economy security and information warfare—reflects the evolving, multi-domain nature of internal security threats facing India, extending beyond traditional terrorism to non-traditional and hybrid threats including sub-aerial systems (drones) and bio-security risks.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Multi Agency Centre (MAC)', mentioned in the context of India's internal security architecture, is primarily concerned with:
options: Coordinating disaster relief operations among states
Fusion and sharing of intelligence among security and law enforcement agencies
Regulating cross-border trade and customs enforcement
prelims_questions.explanation: MAC was strengthened after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks as the nodal platform for real-time intelligence sharing and fusion among central and state security agencies to counter terrorism and other national security threats.

prelims_questions.question: The PRAHAAR scheme, referred to in the National Security Strategies Conference 2026, is associated with which of the following?
options: Countering radicalisation and terrorism at the grassroots level
prelims_questions.explanation: PRAHAAR is a Ministry of Home Affairs scheme/training initiative aimed at building capacity among police forces to counter radicalisation and terrorism.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the changing nature of internal security threats in India, with reference to cyber-crime, proxy warfare, and emerging domains such as sub-aerial systems and the blue economy. What institutional mechanisms exist to address these multi-dimensional challenges?

Examine the role of intelligence fusion centres like the Multi Agency Centre (MAC) in strengthening India's counter-terrorism framework. What further reforms are needed to enhance inter-agency coordination?

related_articles.relationship: The NSS Conference explicitly directs implementation of the PRAHAAR scheme, which was launched as India's National Counter Terrorism Policy & Strategy and is the same initiative referenced in the new release's counter-terrorism discussions.
